citation.title: A dynamic state observer for real-time reconstruction of the tokamak plasma profile state and disturbances
citation.authors: Federico Felici; Marco de Baar; Maarten Steinbuch
citation.venue: 2014 American Control Conference (ACC), Portland, Oregon, USA

topic: EKF observer combining a RAPTOR transport model (psi, electron Te) with simulated diagnostics; random-walk state disturbances
own_question: Can a model-based dynamic observer reconstruct coupled current and electron temperature profiles, and their disturbances, from noisy measurements over time? The comparison point is single-time equilibrium inversion.
actual_method_and_evidence: Spline-discretized coupled PDEs give a 34-state nonlinear model, augmented with 34 random-walk disturbances. An EKF uses analytic Jacobians. Covariances are hand-designed for spatial smoothness. Linear time-varying observability is analyzed via a Gramian along one trajectory. Evidence comes only from simulations of a TCV-like ramp-up with artificial Gaussian noise (Table I sigmas): a nominal case, injected actuator-power disturbances, and 30% higher thermal conductivity. Results are qualitative, shown in figures; no quantitative error metrics are given. Real-time deployment is described as underway, not demonstrated.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Prior work has framed tokamak profile reconstruction as dynamic state estimation using time evolution, rather than single-time inversion. One example is an EKF on a physics transport model with additive disturbance states.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: p.1 abstract; p.4 Sec. III-A, Eqs. (18)-(27)
claim_checks.qualification: Covers electron Te and poloidal flux, not impurity CES Ti. Demonstrated in simulation only.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Innovation whiteness and zero-mean behavior have been proposed as diagnostics of observer quality and model mismatch.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: p.6 Sec. IV-A; p.6-7 Sec. IV-B2/B3
claim_checks.qualification: This is the authors' proposal, illustrated in simulation. It is not a validated fault detector.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Inputs are synthetic measurements (Te and iota at 6 points, psi_b, Ip) assumed available at each time step. There is no report latency or arrival-time model. The target is the true simulated state, not CES reports. The authors report RAPTOR at under 5 ms per step in MATLAB on a PC; this is offline timing.
validation_if_relevant: Synthetic data from the same model family, with one perturbed-parameter test. No experimental data, held-out data, or baselines such as hold or interpolation.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim this paper addresses ion or impurity temperature, CES, BES, or ECEI.
Do not claim real-time deployment or experimental validation.
Do not cite it as evidence that observers outperform interpolation or hold baselines.
Do not generalize it to all prior work being causal or electron-only.
Do not take the 5 ms figure as achieved control-system latency.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: It is a concise causal-estimation precedent for the background section, contrasting model-based observers with our data-driven nowcasting of reported CES values. Its scope differs from ours: simulated electron and current profiles.
